A_target.statement:
Let $F$ be a [[Definition:Polynomial Functor|polynomial functor]] given by the constructors of an [[Definition:Inductive Type|inductive datatype]] $\mu F$.
Then $\mu F$ is the [[Definition:Initial Algebra|initial $F$-algebra]], and structural recursion out of $\mu F$ is uniquely defined.

B_source.statement:
Let $I$ be an [[Definition:Initial Object|initial object]] of a [[Definition:Metacategory|category]] $\mathbf C$.
Then for every object $X$ of $\mathbf C$ there is exactly one [[Definition:Morphism|morphism]] $I \to X$.

substitutions.the objects of the category: algebras for the signature functor, that is, types with constructor operations
substitutions.the initial object: the inductive datatype with its constructors
substitutions.the unique map out of the initial object: the function defined by structural recursion

derived.uniqueness of the map out: uniqueness of the recursively defined function
derived.the initial algebra structure map being: the datatype is a fixed point of its signature functor

object_map.reformulation: Package the constructors into one operation so that the datatype becomes an initial algebra, hence a fixed point of the signature.

validity_conditions: Algebras for the signature functor are exactly types equipped with operations matching the constructor arities, so initiality is a statement about recursion.
Existence of the unique map is the recursion principle and uniqueness is the uniqueness of recursively defined functions, which together give the induction principle.
Lambek's lemma shows the structure map of an initial algebra is invertible, so the datatype is genuinely a fixed point of the functor rather than merely mapping into one.
proof_plan: Present the constructors as a single [[Definition:Functor|functor]]; for lists, $\map F X = 1 + A \times X$.
Consider [[Definition:F-Algebra|$F$-algebras]] $\alpha: \map F X \to X$, that is, types carrying the constructor operations.

The datatype $\mathsf {in}: \map F {\mu F} \to \mu F$ is the [[Definition:Initial Object|initial]] $F$-algebra.
The unique morphism to any algebra $\alpha$ is the fold, which is the structurally recursive function defined by $\alpha$.
